knowledge:
- key_parameters: cyList=A list of graphNEL objects representing raw pathways to be parsed ;; parseNetworks=Logical, if TRUE, parses the raw networks into gene-level networks ;; entrezOnly=Logical, if TRUE, only keeps nodes that have an Entrez Gene ID ;; propagateReg=Logical, if FALSE, prevents the propagation of regulation edges (passed to parseNCINetwork)
- alternatives: KEGGgraph is mentioned as an alternative for importing and manipulating KEGG pathways from XML files.
- when_to_use: Use when you need to incorporate NCI Pathway Interaction Database pathways (Nature-curated or BioCarta) as prior network structures (graphNEL objects) for downstream statistical analyses, such as identifying differentially expressed pathways.
- pitfalls: None of the pathways imported from Reactome contain nodes associated with Entrez IDs, so parsing them with entrezOnly=TRUE will result in empty graphs. Loading networks directly from Cytoscape is slow and requires Cytoscape and specific plugins (CyREST and RCy3). Some NCI-PID networks cannot be loaded due to BioPAX parsing errors or RCy3 reading limitations.

workflows.name: pathway_loading_and_parsing
workflows.intent: Load raw NCI pathways and parse them into gene-level graphNEL objects for downstream analysis and visualization.
input: NCI.demo.cyList (a list of raw graphNEL objects representing pathways)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the NCIgraph package and the raw pathway data. ;; 2. Parse the raw pathways to keep only Entrez-ID-associated nodes and optionally propagate regulation. ;; 3. Visualize the raw and parsed pathways using Rgraphviz.
workflows.code:
library(NCIgraph)
data("NCIgraphVignette", package="NCIgraph")
grList <- getNCIPathways(cyList=NCI.demo.cyList, parseNetworks=TRUE, entrezOnly=TRUE, verbose=TRUE)$pList
library('Rgraphviz')
graph <- NCI.demo.cyList[[1]]
gNames <- unlist(lapply(graph@nodeData@data,FUN=function(e) e$biopax.name))
names(gNames) <- nodes(graph)
graph <- layoutGraph(graph)
nodeRenderInfo(graph) <- list(label=gNames, cex=0.75)
renderGraph(graph)  
graph <- grList[[1]]
gNames <- unlist(lapply(graph@nodeData@data,FUN=function(e) unique(e$biopax.xref.ENTREZGENE)))
names(gNames) <- nodes(graph)
graph <- layoutGraph(graph)
nodeRenderInfo(graph) <- list(label=gNames, cex=0.75)
renderGraph(graph)
